sites.name: M/V HONDIUS
sites.desc: Dutch-flagged polar vessel en route to Granadilla cargo port, Tenerife; ETA early hours Sunday 10 May. Will NOT pier-dock — passengers transferred by inflatable/tender boats to isolated cordoned quayside after repatriation flights confirmed ready. All 147 aboard (87 passengers, 60 crew, 24 nationalities) asymptomatic as of 09 May per Oceanwide. German woman's body remains aboard; WHO coordinating safe storage and transport. Disembarkation window closes Tuesday due to worsening weather. Canary Islands govt has requested ship proceed to Netherlands for decontamination after pax disembark.

sites.name: USHUAIA / ARGENTINA ROUTE
sites.desc: Confirmed source investigation zone. Dutch index couple (Cases 1 & 2) conducted 4-month birdwatching road trip (27 Nov 2025–01 Apr 2026) spanning Chile, Uruguay, and Argentina, crossing the Chile-Argentina border multiple times. WHO working hypothesis is exposure occurred during Argentina/Chile leg pre-cruise. Malbrán Institute team had not yet departed for Ushuaia as of 07 May; rodent trapping to begin 'coming days.' Argentina confirmed no cruise-linked cases domestically; no Ushuaia hantavirus cases in recent decades. National tally: 101 infections since Jun 2025, roughly double prior year.

sites.name: SAINT HELENA
sites.desc: 30 passengers disembarked 24 Apr (includes Dutch index male body and Dutch widow who later died in Johannesburg). Swiss confirmed male case also disembarked here. NICD and UKHSA contact-tracing 82 passengers + 6 crew from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight ongoing. 7 UK nationals from St Helena disembarkation traced by UKHSA; 2 self-isolating in UK. Disembarkees from 12 countries departed before hantavirus was confirmed (02 May).

sites.name: JOHANNESBURG
sites.desc: Case 2 (Dutch widow, 69, PCR+) died at Johannesburg hospital 26 Apr — sole PCR-confirmed Andes virus death. Case 3 (British guide Martin Anstee, 56, PCR+) treated at Johannesburg ICU, condition improved and subsequently redirected to Netherlands. NICD contact-traced 65+ contacts from 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight (82 pax + 6 crew). Asymptomatic South African woman (briefly in Barcelona) confirmed located and monitored in South Africa.

sites.name: AMSTERDAM / NIJMEGEN
sites.desc: British Case 3 (Anstee, 56) redirected to Netherlands after condition improved en route to Tenerife. Dutch crew member (41, confirmed) being treated at Radboud UMC Nijmegen. Netherlands lab PCR-confirmed postmortem that German woman died of Andes virus. KLM flight attendant admitted Amsterdam UMC 07 May with mild symptoms — tested NEGATIVE 08 May. RIVM: 3 people with symptoms tested after KL592 contact — 2 NEGATIVE, 1 result pending. GGD tracing KL592 passengers. Four medical staff (1 Italian, 3 Dutch) remain aboard Hondius.

sites.name: LONDON
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed 2 British nationals PCR+ (one transferred to Netherlands, one originally treated South Africa) and flagged a 3rd suspected case on Tristan da Cunha. UK repatriation flight arranged for 19 passengers and 4 crew from Tenerife; FCDO/UKHSA RDT pre-positioned. Asymptomatic returning Britons to isolate up to 45 days per UKHSA guidance.

sites.name: PARIS
sites.desc: Eight French nationals identified as close contacts of confirmed case on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight. One reporting mild symptoms, isolated pending PCR results. French health ministry coordinating diagnostics and quarantine measures.

sites.name: ZURICH
sites.desc: PCR-confirmed male passenger (one of 30 who disembarked St Helena 24 Apr) self-presented to doctor after symptom onset; confirmed Andes virus at University Hospital Zurich — confirmed 06 May. Wife (also on trip) asymptomatic and isolating. Swiss authorities conducting additional contact tracing.

sites.name: BERLIN / DÜSSELDORF
sites.desc: German woman died on board 02 May (fever/malaise onset 28 Apr, developed pneumonia). Netherlands laboratory postmortem PCR returned Andes virus positive; WHO notes cause of death still officially under investigation. Asymptomatic 65-year-old German contact evacuated 06 May to Netherlands, subsequently returned to Germany (Düsseldorf) for monitoring. RKI contact tracing active.

sites.name: ALICANTE
sites.desc: 32-year-old woman hospitalized in negative-pressure isolation with respiratory symptoms consistent with hantavirus; was a passenger on same 25 Apr St Helena–Johannesburg flight as deceased Dutch woman. Health Secretary Padilla noted this is 'a pretty unlikely case' given seating distance. PCR results pending as of 09 May. Valencia Regional Health coordinating.

sites.name: TENERIFE
sites.desc: Hondius to anchor offshore Granadilla cargo port early Sunday 10 May — will NOT dock pier-side. Dockworkers threatened blockade; final plan confirms offshore anchor, inflatable boats to isolated cordoned quayside, then guarded buses to airport. Disembarkation window closes Tuesday; weather worsens from Monday. WHO/CDC/UKHSA/ECDC/RIVM teams pre-positioned. Canary Islands government requested ship sail on to Netherlands for decontamination post-disembarkation.

sites.name: MADRID
sites.desc: Gómez Ulla Military Hospital fully activated to receive 14 Spanish Hondius passengers under quarantine protocol. PCR on arrival + Day 7; twice-daily temperature checks; single rooms, no visitors. Biosecurity equivalent to Ebola/COVID-19 protocols; 60–80 additional staff recruited. High-Level Isolation Unit (UAAN, 22nd floor) on standby for any passenger developing symptoms.

sites.name: BARCELONA
sites.desc: South African woman (asymptomatic flight contact of Dutch deceased) spent approximately one week in Barcelona before returning to South Africa. Located and confirmed asymptomatic. No local transmission identified.

sites.name: TRISTAN DA CUNHA
sites.desc: UKHSA confirmed suspected hantavirus case (08 May): British passenger who disembarked Hondius during 13–15 Apr stop; developed symptoms and sought medical advice. Spouse isolating. 6 additional guests joined Hondius at Tristan da Cunha per Oceanwide, expanding contact tracing scope. Patient currently on island; UKHSA assessing remotely. Ship stopped here before outbreak was identified.

sites.name: SINGAPORE
sites.desc: Two male residents (aged 67 and 65) isolated in government facility; both disembarked Hondius at St Helena and were on 25 Apr Airlink St Helena–Johannesburg flight with confirmed case. One has mild rhinorrhea, second asymptomatic. PCR results pending. CDA notified 04–05 May; public risk in Singapore assessed as low. Both residents arrived Singapore by 04 May.

sites.name: ONTARIO
sites.desc: Two Ontario residents self-isolating — Hondius passengers who returned home. Four Canadians total remain aboard vessel awaiting Tenerife evacuation. PHAC coordinating monitoring per 07 May government statement.

sites.name: QUEBEC
sites.desc: One Quebec resident self-isolating — not a Hondius passenger but shared homebound flight with two Canadian Hondius disembarkees. Asymptomatic; PHAC monitoring active.

sites.name: ARIZONA
sites.desc: ADHS monitoring one returning passenger under 42-day observation. Asymptomatic as of 09 May. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 5–6 states per CDC. CDC notified ADHS 05 May; public risk assessed as very low.

sites.name: CALIFORNIA
sites.desc: CDPH coordinating with local health officials to monitor one returned Hondius traveler via daily temperature checks and symptom assessment. A second California resident remains aboard ship and will transit Tenerife to Nebraska NQU via CDC-escorted State Dept charter. No California residents reported ill or infected as of 09 May.

sites.name: GEORGIA
sites.desc: Georgia DPH monitoring two residents who returned from Hondius. Both in good health with no signs of infection as of 08 May per GDPH statement to Live Science. Following CDC recommendations.

sites.name: TEXAS
sites.desc: Texas DSHS monitoring two returning Hondius passengers. Both asymptomatic. Part of domestic US monitoring cohort across 5–6 states.

sites.name: VIRGINIA
sites.desc: VDH monitoring one returning Hondius passenger. Asymptomatic. President Trump stated 08 May the US situation is 'very much, we hope, under control.' CDC classified response as Level-3 (lowest emergency activation tier). Five states — AZ, CA, GA, TX, VA — monitoring at least 7 early-disembarkees per CNN 08 May.

sites.name: NEW JERSEY
sites.desc: NJ health authorities monitoring two individuals with potential post-disembarkation exposure to a Hondius passenger. Neither symptomatic as of 09 May. Part of the broader US monitoring cohort per ABC News reporting.

sites.name: NEBRASKA
sites.desc: Nebraska Medicine / UNMC National Quarantine Unit (NQU) fully staffed and activated. CDC team pre-deployed to Offutt AFB, Bellevue. 17 American Hondius passengers to arrive via CDC-escorted State Dept biocontainment charter from Tenerife after Sunday docking. NQU medical director Dr. Wadman confirmed all 17 are asymptomatic; anyone developing symptoms to be moved to Biocontainment Unit. Dr. Michael Ash (Nebraska Medicine CEO): 'We are prepared for situations exactly like this.'

sites.name: MANILA
sites.desc: 38 Filipino crew members aboard Hondius; Philippines DOH confirmed none are currently ill as of 08 May. In close coordination with vessel operator and international authorities. Monitoring continues pending Tenerife disembarkation and subsequent repatriation.

sites.name: DUBLIN
sites.desc: Two Irish nationals confirmed aboard Hondius per RTE. Ireland is among nine EU/EEA nationalities on board per ECDC briefing. Irish Dept of Health coordinating with ECDC and WHO; returning Irish nationals to quarantine per national protocol.

sites.name: PRAIA
sites.desc: Hondius anchored off Praia 03–06 May; departed 19:15 local 06 May for Tenerife. Three medevac patients evacuated here 06 May — two flew to Amsterdam (received by specialist teams at Schiphol), third plane made unscheduled refueling stop at Gran Canaria after Morocco refused permission. Cape Verde assessed unable to handle full passenger evacuation — basis for WHO requesting Tenerife docking. 2,500 Argentine diagnostic kits dispatched to five countries.
